title:
One proof before sleep.
One after you wake.
sub: A daily reasoning ritual that replaces the feed.
say: Nightproof. One logic problem before sleep, one after you wake.

caption: Tonight's proof is one problem — not a feed.
say: The last thing most students open at night is a feed. Nightproof opens one reasoning problem instead, chosen from the date so it cannot be re-rolled.

caption: One careful read. No timer, no re-roll.
say: A LEET-style argument, five options, no timer. This is the skill the exam actually rewards: reading one argument carefully, once.

caption: Three lines: what you did, why it fails, what to remember.
say: Miss it, and instead of an answer key you get the trap you fell into, named — in three lines written for that exact option. Not generated at the moment you tap; authored, so it can never invent an explanation.

caption: The mistakes become a map of where you leak points.
say: A week of answers becomes a profile. Eight traps on a radar, the two you are leaking points on, and a drill for each.

caption: In the morning, the app locks itself until you think.
say: And in the morning the app locks itself, for the first ninety minutes after your alarm, until the proof is answered or its reasoning is read.

caption: 60 items, 8 named traps, English and Korean.
say: Sixty items in English and Korean, written with G P T 6 Astra, every answer key re-read by Claude Fable 5.1 as a second examiner, and fifty six tests passing in a real browser.
